drug_class: Combination Rho Kinase Inhibitor and Prostaglandin Analog (eye drops)
purpose: This eye drop is used to lower the pressure inside your eyes. It is prescribed for people with glaucoma or a condition called ocular hypertension, where the pressure in the eye is too high. Keeping eye pressure under control helps protect your vision and prevents damage to your optic nerve.
how_it_works: Your eye constantly makes and drains a fluid that keeps it healthy. When that fluid does not drain well enough, pressure builds up and can damage your sight. This medicine works in two ways at once — one ingredient (netarsudil) helps fluid drain better and reduces how much fluid is made, while the other ingredient (latanoprost) opens up a different drainage pathway to let even more fluid out, together lowering your eye pressure more effectively than either one alone.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects happen right in the eye and include redness of the eye or eyelids, small visible blood vessels on the white part of the eye, eye discomfort or pain, deposits on the cornea (the clear front part of your eye), and blurry vision right after putting in the drops. Your iris (the colored part of your eye) may slowly turn more brown over time, and your eyelashes may grow longer, thicker, or darker.
warnings: Do not use these drops if you are allergic to any of the ingredients. Tell your doctor if you wear contact lenses — you should remove them before putting in the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in. Let your doctor know about all other eye drops or medicines you take. If you notice sudden vision changes, eye pain, or signs of an eye infection, contact your doctor right away. Avoid touching the dropper tip to your eye or any surface to keep it clean and germ-free.
typical_dosing: Use one drop in the affected eye or eyes once every evening, at bedtime. Try to use it at the same time each night. Do not use more than one drop per day, as using it more often will not help and may cause more side effects. If you miss a dose, just continue with your next scheduled evening dose — do not double up.
